findings.what: canonicalPair gives wrong answers, without any warning, on a finite board with more than 10000 symmetries. It takes symmetries(d.board) with the default cap CAPS.relabellingsDefault = 10000, and symmetries returns no truncated flag, so the minimum is taken over only part of the group. Two pairs in the same class then get different representatives, which breaks the defining property in SPEC 5.5. The fragment says canonicalPair 'works on every finite board, in several pieces included' (decisions/P6-A2.md:16). Only custom boards can reach this (at least 8 nodes, for example 8 isolated nodes). T13 uses named boards only, where there are at most 6 symmetries.
findings.evidence: node --experimental-strip-types --import scratch/loader.mjs scratch/cap_engine.mjs on fromAdjacency(8x8 zeros): symmetries 10000; canonicalPair(black [6,7], id) = {black:[0,2]}; canonicalPair(black [0,1], id) = {black:[0,1]} (same class, different representatives). Oracle python3 scratch/cap_oracle.py: 40320 automorphisms, canonical_pair = ((0,1),(0..7)). On 9 nodes, black [7] with tau (0 8): engine {black:[1],tau:[3,1,2,0,4,5,6,7,8]}, oracle ((0,),(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,7)).
findings.specRef: SPEC 5.5 'apply every symmetry g of the board'; CLAUDE.md 'Every enumeration has a cap and returns {items, truncated}'
findings.proposedFix: Ask for symmetries(board, CAPS.relabellingsDefault + 1). If more than the cap come back, throw an EngineError (or RangeError) that names the cap, rather than returning a pair that is not canonical. Add a test on 8 isolated nodes and correct the fragment's sentence.

Eight non-equivalent mutants of my own pass all 137 p6b tests, yet each disagrees with the oracle on ranks 9 to 16. The engine itself agrees with the oracle there (see checked).

findings.what: Adding realForms, cartanLabels and restrictedTypes to the single names.json made the browser chunk that T10 loads lazily about 7.5 times larger. The reason is that typesetNames.ts imports the default export of the whole file. npm run size does not see this, because the chunk loads after the first interaction. The cost is extra download and parse on the first board change, and T13 and T14 will hit the same trap if they import the whole file.

notes: No blocker or major. Every value the four functions return agrees with the oracle and the golden file, at rank 8 and below and up to rank 16.

Q1, coverage of satake_examples: MERGE already ruled (DECISIONS 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.1, P6-A5, and stage 6.1b, P6-A2'). My reading: the purpose of CONTRACTS 3 holds. The key is registered by a file that compares it, and between the two files every compared field is checked (reasons is documentation by rule 6). No change needed. The same holds for satake, registered by p6b-satake-records.

Q2, matchCatalogue on an unnamed board: SPEC 5.4 and 6.4 are silent, and 6.4 organises the catalogue by board name. A RangeError (a usage error) is better than [], because 5.4's 'none' means 'not admissible' and would mislead. The matrix check the agent added is needed and should be kept as a plan addition: named restricted boards and some fold results carry a name with their matrix in orbit order, and without the check their positions would be read in Bourbaki order. Its message 'built by boardFromName' is slightly inaccurate, because a standard-order fold result is accepted.
Q3, error classes on names: NotABoard on unknown names, as boardFromName gives everywhere in the engine, and NotFiniteType on affine, twisted and preset names, by 5.6. Agreed.

Q4, section names and Cartan-label TeX (\text{A III}): the SPEC fixes neither, and the result renders upright, as the tables print the labels. Acceptable. MERGE should confirm the names and steer consumers to import one section (finding 3).

Q5, affine and twisted names: SPEC 7.3 counts 'boards' among the names with a fixed spelling and says 'the board pickers' look them up. Those pickers show affine and twisted boards (T4, T15, T16), so a strict reading wants these names in names.json eventually. That would change P0-A3's katex.test.ts assertion that texOfName('A4~') throws. P6-A2's instruction excluded them, so this should be a separate task assigned by MERGE (T4's verdict.ts writes its own MathML for now).
Q6, README against the roster JSON for admissible_counts: the JSON and the instruction agree, and MERGE recorded P6-A2 as the registrant. Only build-plan/README.md:174 is stale.
The agent's deviations (shape checks before guards; the matrix check in matchCatalogue) follow MERGE's engine-wide ruling and are sound.

Small input-handling points, none worth a finding: satakeRecord(['A3'], entry) succeeds with dynkin_type ['A3'], because boardFromName coerces the name through a regex; the TypeScript signature excludes this. A diagram whose board is {n:3} throws TypeError, not RangeError, as P6-A1's functions also do. Non-number entries in tau or black get the message 'outside 0..n-1'.
